mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 5% in the month prior to the decision is associated with a short-term negative S&P 500 20-day forward return due to reduced risk-free discounting of future cash flows.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5% in the prior month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are non-negative in at least 80% of post-tightening windows, or FEDFUNDS volatility is below historical norms during the period.

mechanism_narrative: Rising unemployment (PAYEMS) below 5% in the prior month coincides with a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return as labor market weakness prompts equity risk premium expansion.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS falls below 5,000 in prior month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in >50% of similar labor weakens periods, or the unemployment rate recovers rapidly within 2 months.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly surge in home sales (HOUST) exceeding 2% year-over-year predicts a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as it signals resilient consumer demand and upward earnings revisions.
failure_condition: No significant correlation between HOUST spikes and 20-day forward returns in 3 consecutive recovery phases.

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive decline in industrial production (INDPRO) of at least 3% in the prior two months predicts a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return as it indicates weakening manufacturing momentum.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls for two consecutive months by >3%
failure_condition: INDPRO recovers without a corresponding S&P 500 forward loss in analogous contraction regimes.

mechanism_narrative: When the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) unexpectedly rises by more than 0.5% in a month, the S&P 500 5-day forward return is negative due to market anticipation of future rate hikes.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are non-negative in 70% of similar inflation surprise events.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% triggers a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as it signals labor market tightening and reduced recession risk.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses below 4% in a single month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain flat or negative during subsequent tightening phases without wage growth.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in both retail sales (PAYEMS) and home sales (HOUST) by at least 3% in the prior month indicate dual demand channels, predicting a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS + HOUST both rise by >3% in the same month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are non-positive in 3 consecutive dual-demand acceleration events.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in consumer spending (measured by a 4-week moving average of GDPC1 falling by 4% or more) predicts a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return as it reflects weakening aggregate demand.
regime_hint: early stage of consumer spending contraction
failure_condition: No significant negative 20-day forward returns accompany such GDPC1 declines in non-recessionary supply shocks.
